Priya, thanks for the prompt notes and for the CSV. Attached is the short SLO/options PDF with three recommended configurations and the core levers called out. Highlights below (ballpark figures).

Key latency/cost levers and expected impact:
1) Continuous batching (runtime):
   - Keeps GPU utilization high by batching in-flight requests; improves throughput and reduces per-token cost.
   - Tradeoff: batching window increases tail latency if not combined with priority routing. At your concurrency (~120) we expect batching to lower per-token cost by ~20-30% while keeping 95p within target with a 15-25 ms batching delay budget.
2) Prefix / KV caching:
   - For chat sessions with repeated prompts or shared system-prefixes, prefix cache can serve many tokens without re-computation.
   - Can reduce effective compute by 10-40% depending on reuse. Good fit if users keep context windows or templates.
3) Quantization profiles (INT8 / mixed precision):
   - INT8 quantization offers ~2x memory reduction and ~1.5-2x throughput improvement on compatible kernels.
   - Slight quality delta vs FP16 for some instruction-heavy prompts; we recommend running a small eval on your prompt set.
4) Model variants:
   - Primary: redwood-13b (best quality) — higher cost/GPU memory.
   - Cost-optimized: redwood-7b-int8 or redwood-13b-quant (quantized variant) — similar perceived quality for many conversational flows, much lower cost.
5) Smart routing + fallback:
   - Route latency-sensitive traffic to lower-latency, smaller variants; route high-quality or complex prompts to 13b. Automated fallback if a variant is overloaded.

Ballpark configs (per 1M tokens / monthly projection) in the attached PDF — short summary:
- Hosted small (hosted multi-tenant): good for initial pilot, uses quantized 7b, continuous batching + cache enabled. Estimated cost: low; 95p latency around 120-180ms in our benchmarks for similar profiles.
- Hosted optimized: hosted with reserved bursts, 13b-quant, aggressive caching. Better quality, moderate cost; 95p ~110-150ms.
- Dedicated reserved: dedicated GPU pool (reserved), 13b FP16, tight batching control, and priority routing. Best latency headroom and predictable SLOs (95p < 120ms) — higher monthly commitment.

Canary/pilot suggestion:
- Start with a hosted optimized config on a small percentage (5-10%) of traffic for 1-2 weeks. Run A/B with quality evals on the same prompt set. If metrics pass, ramp to 25% and then to full.
